pin.glyphBox: the middle 55% of the pin — place the 64u viewBox at 55% of pin diameter, centred

style.notes: no silhouette twins — the pin is the ground
style.silhouetteRule: each marker must be distinguishable with fill stripped — only mk-necropolises is arch-topped; statues is a shouldered torso, dungeons a flat-topped framed door, encounters a figure whose staff crosses the outline
style.colourRule: monochrome-safe silhouettes, but saturated accent colour where the subject is genuinely hot or precious — lava (--mk-lava), mineral water rim (--mk-heat), gilt hilts (--mk-gold/--mk-brass). Accent never carries the silhouette; it identifies within it. Coloured LINES (lava tongues, steam, beams, falling water, the swirl, staves) are stroked in the accent with fill:none; coloured MASSES (cone, plume, pool rim, blade, hilt) are filled with the accent and stroked in --sm-ink. Never fill an open path with an accent.
style.framing: every glyph is centred on (32,32) and fills roughly 44–56u of the 64u box, so no marker renders smaller than its neighbours in the pin. When authoring an arch with a quadratic, remember the apex is 0.25*p0 + 0.5*ctrl + 0.25*p1 — not the control point; solve the control for the apex you want. For any glyph authored inside a rotated group, fit it by its POST-transform bbox — rotation inflates the extent (a 60×40u shape at 20° spans ~70×58u), so authored coordinates that look in-range can still be clipped by the symbol box.
style.projection: markers are drawn in ELEVATION (side view), unlike the settlemaker map symbols which are top-down. Never reuse a radially symmetric map generator here — a conifer is tapering tiers, a palm has fronds in the upper hemisphere only.
